title: Add an unofficial user repository to pacman
summary: Unofficial repositories provide pre-built packages from the AUR or other community sources. You must manually add them to your pacman configuration file and refresh the database.
prerequisites: Identify the repository name and server URL from the Arch Wiki or maintainer's page

steps.explain: Open the pacman configuration file with a text editor (e.g., nano or vim) as root.

Add the repository section at the end of the file. Replace <REPO_NAME> with the repository name (e.g., 'chaotic-aur') and <SERVER_URL> with the server address provided by the maintainer. If the repository is unsigned, you may also need to add 'SigLevel = PackageOptional' inside the section.
Save and exit the editor (Ctrl+O, Enter, Ctrl+X in nano).
Refresh the package database to recognize the new repository.

rollback.explain: Remove the repository section from /etc/pacman.conf and run 'sudo pacman -Sy' again.

warnings: Unofficial repositories are not tested by Arch developers. Use them at your own risk.
Unsigned repositories can be vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks if HTTP is used. Prefer HTTPS and signed repositories.
